descs: Reed and black water, gray on gray, and the smell of standing water.

spots.name: The Sunk Fence
spots.desc: Fence posts march into black water and keep going under it, some farmer's boundary from before the fen took this ground.

spots.name: Dike's End
spots.desc: The ground firms and rises toward a dike; north, drier land climbs on toward Hollowbrook. South, the fen closes back in.

spots.name: Eel-Trap Row
spots.desc: A dozen woven eel-traps hang from a rope strung between posts, half of them torn open and empty.

spots.name: Widow's Weir
spots.desc: A stone weir, moss-slick, channels the black water into a chattering fall barely a foot high. Someone still maintains it, badly.

spots.name: Rush Bank
spots.desc: Rushes taller than a man crowd the bank, cut through by a single narrow track of trodden mud. Wild mint grows rank where the ground stays drier.

spots.name: Sunken Howe
spots.desc: A low mound breaks the reed-flat, turf grown thick and dark. A black doorway shows in its flank, half-choked with silt.

spots.name: Drowned Orchard
spots.desc: Fruit trees stand dead to the waist in black water, bare branches holding their shape years after the roots gave up on it.

spots.name: The Reed-Cutter's Camp
spots.desc: A one-room hut on a spit of drier ground, reed bundled in stacks outside it taller than the roof itself.

spots.name: Heron Reach
spots.desc: A line of herons stands in the shallows, so still you take them for dead branches until one of them blinks.

spots.name: The Last Dry Ground
spots.desc: Reed gives way to firm footing here; west the ground rises dry toward the causeway and the Vale beyond it. East, only water.

spots.name: Mudflat Crossing
spots.desc: A stretch of gray mudflat, pocked with footprints going every direction, none of them recent.

spots.name: The Drowned Nave's Roof
spots.desc: A chapel roof breaks the black water like a whale's back, moss-slick and cracked open along the ridge. Something under it hums, low, just past hearing.

spots.name: Bell-Rope Reeds
spots.desc: Reeds grow unnaturally straight here, in a ring, as if something below keeps them that way. The water at the center never quite goes still.

spots.name: Stilt-Shadow
spots.desc: Reedholm's roofs show east through the reeds, close now, nets strung rail to rail between the houses.

spots.name: Cairn in the Reeds
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones, half sunk, older than anything else standing in this fen. No one has left an offering here in a long time.

spots.name: The Flood-Watch
spots.desc: A stone tower leans but holds, the only thing in the fen taller than the reeds. Its door hangs open on one hinge.

spots.name: The Long Gap
spots.desc: Open water stretches wide here, the reed line broken clean through, as if something once dragged a great weight across it.
spots.brief: A wide break in the reeds.

spots.name: The Eel-Run
spots.desc: The bank here is undercut, a black opening low over the waterline, wide enough to duck into if the water's low.

spots.name: Trapper's Blind
spots.desc: A hunter's blind of woven reed, collapsed at one corner, aimed out over water where nothing has moved in years.

spots.name: The Milestone
spots.desc: A stone marker leans in the mud, its carved word worn past reading. Whatever it once pointed toward, the fen has swallowed the road as well as the name.

spots.name: Cutter's Path
spots.desc: A narrow path of laid reed-bundles, sunk half into the mud, the only dry footing for a long stretch either way.

spots.name: Shingle's Edge
spots.desc: Reed gives way to shingle underfoot, salt cutting through the standing water smell. South, a road climbs toward the coast.

spots.name: Gull Roost
spots.desc: Gulls have taken over a stand of dead trees, screaming at nothing in particular. Their droppings have killed what little green was left.

onEnter: Something surfaces beside you, gray and dripping, before you've even heard it move.

vars.NAME: The Flood-Watch
vars.VIEW: the whole fen spreads flat and gray, Reedholm's roofs east and the coast a pale line south

vars.NAME: The Eel-Run
vars.BEAST: a fen-eel thick as a leg

fd_bog_hide.name: a strip of bog-thing hide
fd_bog_hide.hint: the eel-trader might pay to know what's tearing up her traps

fd_herbs.name: fen-mint, gathered wild
fd_herbs.hint: eat it to ease a wound

fx: Bitter and sharp. It clears the head and eases the ache.

fd_cairn_ward.name: a corroded ward-coin
fd_cairn_ward.hint: old, and worth something to the right buyer

fd_bog_thing.name: bog-thing
fd_bog_thing.desc: Gray-hided and too many-jointed, dripping black water, more animal than anything with a name.
onDeath: It comes apart into mud and old gray hide before it even finishes falling. One piece of hide holds its shape.
